Upon graduation from University of Hong Kong, I had considered several life trajectories, two determining factors weighed in my decision: Hong Kong 97 and my life-long goal of understanding our world from within and from without.  
Possible Life trajectories after Graduation from HKU.  
1. Worked in Hong Kong Government as an Administrative Officer (one of those most coveted jobs among non-professional university graduates).  It was an opportunity I dismissed early on based on the following consideration (I passed the written examination and was offered an interview):
	1. I had no interest or motivation to pursue a political or bureaucratic career in Hong Kong Government, particularly under the shadow of 1997, despite the financial rewards and prestige associated with the job.  With some honing and adaptations of diplomatic skills, holders of these posts can be promoted to director or even top tier administrators of Hong Kong Government.  I knew quite a few former HKUSU office holders (but not necessarily the most visible political figureheads) had this path planned even before they became an office holder.  They tend not to choose playing any active visible political role in HKUSU though.
	2.  My father worked for a Red-China Bank if background check was conducted, I might have a high chance of disqualification (a surmise only with no empirical evidence).
	I ended up preparing the interview with challenging questions for the interviewers regarding with 97 issues and their own plans to address those, showing no interest to play the interview game.  
2. Enrolled in Clinical Psychology and Worked as Clinical Psychologist (a relatively "easy" path at that time) 
	1. I dismissed that path outright as the burden of dealing with emotional and mental issues of people and their related socio-cultural and family contexts would be unhealthy for mental health.  I simply did not want it to be my life-long occupation.
	2. My decision at that time was reinforced by the death of my friend and my primary school acquaintance, Bill Poon who was also a well versed socio-cultural critic later.  He was a clinical psychologist at that time and died of liver cancer within 4 months after discovery.
3. Worked as a middle/high school teacher ("Graduate Master" university graduate only, another straightforward path) with good reputation, relatively high-pay, a high possibility of promotion to superintendent of a school. 
	1. I did not have interest either.   I knew a few GMs - My cousin and his spouse were GMs, I actually sold the business startup with my Baptist College classmates to a Senior Graduate Master who wanted to start his side business.  I was not the type that would want to teach middle/high school students all life.  
4. Enrolled in the Philosophy Department in Hong Kong University and worked on a thesis of my own interest.  I could also hold full-time jobs such while working towards my Master degree
	1. I actually enrolled with the proposed thesis title: "The Arrow of Time" under Professor Goldstein.
	2.  I withdrew from the Master Program after consideration and hatching of my escape route from Hong Kong.  
5. The Escape Route from Hong Kong.  It was the most uncertain and risky move as I would need to forgo all the well-defined alternative paths and the familiarity of Hong Kong and my friends.
	1. In order to hatch a plan without any financial resources, I would need to get complete financial support from the universities and the disciplines I wanted to focus on.  I worked as a teaching assistant of Psychology Department of the Chinese University of Hong Kong for 2 years while gaining the research/teaching experience and credentials, taking GRE examination and deciding specific areas of psychology I would want to focus on.  My general interest at that time was computational model of cognitive psychology, particularly in the brain and vision.   I read quite a number of books and papers in those years on cybernetics, computational vision and natural computation.  Note that my undergraduate thesis was "Orienting response using dual-task paradigm" so attention theory played an important part in my graduate study as well as future career.
	2. I was accepted by Purdue (Mathematical Psychology), University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign, University of New Mexico at Las Cruz, SUNYAB (with financial assistance in the from of RA, TA or fellowship) and MIT (a telex from department of Natural Computation but no financial assistance can be found).   I was naturally disappointed at not being able to go to MIT. In retrospect, I probably would not survive the program at MIT as I don't have the sufficient mathematical background to do well there.
	3. I eventually went to SUNYAB.  My colleague, Tony Tsoi was already there in the same department in another lab (audio perception).  He is a good friend and offers help, advice and guidance with no hesitation.  Although I initially was placed into Irwin Biederman's lab (visual perception, I would prefer to work under a new assistant professor, Michael Leyton (joint appointment with CS and Psych), whose research area was more aligned with my interest.
